description: Central registry of external methodologies, taxonomies, research, datasets and government guidance used by VIGIL. Registry inclusion records methodological use; it does not imply endorsement or equivalence.

references.title: AI Incident Tracker: Harm Taxonomy
references.use_note: Direction-of-scale and harm-context reference: 1 is Negligible and 5 is Catastrophic. VIGIL does not adopt MIT ratings or categories as incident determinations.

references.title: AI Incident Tracker
references.use_note: Reference for report-level harm review and the tracker relationship to CSET-derived harm categories.

references.title: AI Incident Tracker June 2026 Update
references.use_note: Reference for evidence-bounded reviewer practice, including rating from the raw report and recognising incomplete-report disagreement.

references.title: Adding Structure to AI Harm: An Introduction to CSET's AI Harm Framework
references.publisher: Center for Security and Emerging Technology, Georgetown University
references.use_note: Harm-category and consequence-context reference. VIGIL retains its own operational dimensions and thresholds.

references.title: Federal Incident Notification Guidelines
references.use_note: Reference for separating functional impact from recoverability and assessing business or service impact.

references.title: CISA National Cyber Incident Scoring System
references.use_note: Reference for actual functional impact, information impact, recoverability and cross-sector scope.

references.title: Contingency Planning Guide for Federal Information Systems (SP 800-34 Rev. 1)
references.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
references.use_note: Reference for recovery-time objective and maximum-tolerable-downtime concepts; VIGIL uses evidenced organisational limits when available.

references.title: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2690
references.use_note: Sector-specific operational thresholds inform VIGIL service-impact anchors; they are not universal automatic severity assignments.

references.title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1772
references.use_note: DORA materiality indicators inform operational, duration, client-scope and loss anchors without making VIGIL equivalent to DORA classification.

references.title: Cyber Incident Management Arrangements for Australian Governments
references.publisher: Australian Signals Directorate, Australian Cyber Security Centre
references.use_note: Reference for consequence, national coordination, cross-jurisdiction and critical-infrastructure context.

references.title: Prioritization of Risks from Artificial Intelligence: A Delphi Study of 272 International Experts
references.use_note: Principal external quantitative and cross-domain severity reference informing VIGIL-HIM's five-level anchors. VIGIL owns its operational thresholds, including its explicit financial gap-closing rule; inclusion does not claim equivalence with or endorsement by MIT FutureTech.
